title: Central Avenue after-hours spots and first marijuana
summary: Moore names after-hours places and recalls hanging out with Tyree Glenn, trying marijuana, and leaving his Cadillac parked in the middle of the street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I thought I'd mention some of the experiences about that in the after-hours spots in Los Angeles.
There used to be a place called Ivie Anderson's --
That was named after the Ellington vocalist.
And there are different spots where all musicians hang out. Alex Lovejoy, a joint called The Big-Legged Chicken on Central Avenue. There

was a place called the Bucket of Blood, as well as the famous Club Alabam and I used to hang around with Tyree Glenn, this was during the time that he was playing with Eddie Barefield at the Cotton Club. Eddie Barefield left Cab Calloway to form a band and Tyree was in that band while I was with Charlie Echols in the City of Los Angeles at Billy Patke's Club.

And after each performance, after the night was over at our respective places where we worked, we got together out in Central Avenue and that was my first introduction to drugs, marijuana, and it was considered at the time to be in the in-crowd and I tried it. By golly, that was some years. That was the year and -- ha-ha -- I got high and sat in with most of the musicians around town there, which included Tyree, there was quite a number of guys that -- I remember there was a band at Club Alabam by the name of Lorenzo Flaunois, the piano player -- real, tall fella, had a nice group and Oscar Bradley was the drummer there. And at one time I was so knocked out that I had parked my -- I had a Cadillac -- and I parked in front of the Alabam in the center of Central Avenue -- and it was told to me later, after I woke up the next day that the musicians said, look at ole
